title: Review of c03's size-decay no-turnover finding: replicates on fresh seed 9 (a=2: 26 -> 52 bodies, 23 splits, 0-2 deaths per window; a=5: 26 -> 28, 3 splits, 1-2 deaths)
summary: Fresh seed 9, T=960 (120 frames x 400 steps, as the author), both arms unchanged, read with c03's turnover.py in six windows. a=2: bodies divide in the middle of the run (14 and 6 splits in windows 3-4) and the population grows 26 -> 52, with 0-2 deaths per window and nothing at all in the last window. a=5: division is almost suppressed (26 -> 28, 3 splits) and 1 death after the first window. As on seed 0, the mass-scaled catalyst decay slows growth everywhere instead of killing the largest bodies, so it does not create ongoing turnover.

observations.D: turnover_seed9.txt: a=2 26 -> 52 bodies with 23 splits and 4 deaths in t=960 (0 events in the last window); a=5 26 -> 28 with 3 splits and 2 deaths

seeds_run.result: pass for a=2 and a=5: growth or stasis, 0-2 deaths per window

controls_run.D: a5/seed9 against a2/seed9 (two strengths of the same cost, same seed)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and the same short horizon (T=960); a longer run could still reach a crowded state with deaths. I did not run a=0 (the parent world) on this seed.
